## Incident Report — Skill-Issue-LLM PCAP Forensics
**Capture:** `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,091 frames, ~58 min)

### Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.17.0.99 | Source of all C2/beacon traffic; conv,ip top talker |
| MAC | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 | ARP src for 172.17.0.99 and DHCP client MAC |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (domain: bepositive.com) | NBNS `<00>`/`<20>` records + DHCP `dhcp.option.hostname`, both bound to 172.17.0.99 |
| Logged-in user | afletcher | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic from 172.17.0.99 to the DC |

Domain controller for reference: 172.17.0.17 = WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19 (NBNS/Kerberos realm BEPOSITIVE.COM) — this is normal internal AD traffic, not part of the incident.

### Malware / Activity
Attribution: **behavioral, not signature-confirmed.** No executable payload was captured in cleartext to hash and match against a known family signature, so the family name below is a pattern match, not a certainty.

Behavior observed:
1. At t=153.5s the host opens a TLS 1.3 session to **46.254.34.201:443**, SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (a compromised/malicious Italian small-business site used as a stager — no prior DNS query for this name appears anywhere in the capture, meaning the client connected to a hardcoded IP and sent the SNI value without a visible local lookup, a common loader evasion trait). All traffic on this connection is TLS-encrypted; content cannot be recovered from the pcap.
2. At t=155.9s, ~2.4 seconds after that connection starts, the host begins a persistent HTTP check-in loop that runs for the remainder of the capture: repeated `POST /foots.php` requests to **79.124.78.197:80** (plain HTTP, bare-IP `Host:` header — no domain was ever resolved for this IP either). Each POST carries a pipe-delimited body such as:
   `101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|5LHtVruc|f3f3oMg2lz4XGyHy0LidzFiNvSftke//k+COyrO9aBI=`
   using a spoofed legacy `User-Agent: Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; ...)`. The server always answers with an empty `200 OK` chunked body — no second-stage payload was delivered during the capture window.
3. The same host also hit a pay-per-install "installs tracking" gate on the same server: `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U`, which returned `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`, followed by a `POST /index.php` with an encrypted/binary body.

This combination — a persistent numeric/GUID bot-ID check-in over `foots.php`, a separate affiliate/subid installs-gate on `index.php`, bare-IP HTTP hosting, and a legacy IE7 user-agent — matches the general profile of a **pay-per-install loader/bot (PrivateLoader-class check-in behavior)**. No static sample was recovered in this capture to confirm the exact family via hash or code signature, so this is flagged behavioral, not confirmed.

All other traffic (MSN/Bing/Office 365/Windows Update/Adobe MAU/GoDaddy SSO/connecttest.txt/LDAP-Kerberos-SMB to the DC) is normal Windows/enterprise noise and is not part of the incident.
